newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European markets slide ahead of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European markets slide ahead of U.S. data.

text.p: European share markets slipped from this week's record breaking highs on Wednesday as investors on both sides of the Atlantic cashed in some of their gains ahead of key U.S. prices data.

Wall Street's five point drop to 6,004.78 set the tone in Europe, where the London, France and Frankfurt bourses all went into retreat before the release of September consumer inflation figures at 1230 GMT.
The dollar and bond markets were also on hold ahead of the data, seen as a pointer to what might happen to U.S. interest rates.
The dollar extended Tuesday's rally in early trading but later eased back to around 1.54 marks, although traders said the chart picture remained very bullish.
Benchmark November Brent crude was trading just under $25 a barrel, having traded a little under six-year highs on Tuesday.

Former OPEC secretary-general Subroto forecast oil prices could squeeze even higher if the northern hemisphere winter proves severe and Iraq is unable to return to the world market. London stocks fell steadily through the morning as the market reacted to British economic data and Wall Street.
A stronger-than-expected fall in unemployment, higher earnings numbers and a high figure for public borrowing in September combined to pull shares back from their record close on Tuesday.
By 1115 GMT the FTSE 100 index was off 23.5 points at 4,027.3.

"The figures were disappointing for the bulls but shouldn't come as a surprise for anyone in the real world. The economy can't be the best in Europe and be immune from falling unemployment," said SocGen strategist Andy Hartwill.
"This market is being driven by the perpetual hope that interest rate increases are something you read about in fairy stories rather than happen in the real world."

British satellite broadcaster BSkyB fell 3p to 673-1/2p after cautious comments from BZW following the surge in the stock in recent weeks. Shares in Smiths Industries added 13p to 804-1/2p after full-year results at the top end of forecasts.
German shares also fell through the morning on modest profit-taking.
The DAX index of leading German shares was down 14 points at 2,714, a fall of around half a percent, by lunchtime.
However, carmaker Volkswagen rose in reaction to new General Motors figures, seen as pointing to strength in the car sector.
French stocks opened stable but slipped about six points by midday.
The dollar's recent rally took a breather after probing new peaks in early trading.

"I think all we've seen this morning is the expected bit of profit-taking on the dollar and sterling after what has been, after all, a one-way market for a couple of days," said Peter Wood, a trader at Bank of Boston in London.
Sterling backed off its new 21-month high against the mark at 2.4475, but the robust drop in British unemployment in September helped underpin the pound above 2.44 later.
Traders said they were waiting for the U.S. prices figures for fresh direction for the dollar.

"In some respects it is a no-lose situation for the dollar here because if it's a modest number, asset markets will rise again and, if not, the prospect of higher U.S. interest rates should also buoy the currency," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5396 marks and 112.19 yen, compared with 1.5394 marks and 112.29 yen in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
London - The FTSE index was down 23.5 points at 4,027.3.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 14.09 points at 2,714.36.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 6.18 points at 2,162.10. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $380.80 against $381.00 on Tuesday. Silver was one cent lower at $5.02.
